notes: SAGE PARITY, NOT STATUTORY TRUTH: the R1 125.00 is Sage's flat 25% for its "Temporary/Part time" status. The statutory figure depends on hours (G21 Rev 1 p. 27-28, summary table): required to work at least 22 hours a week is standard employment, taxed on the tables, and R54 000 a year is under the R99 000 threshold, so R0.00; non-standard employment of at least 5 hours a day for less than R394 a day has no employees' tax; non-standard at more than R394 a day, or under 5 hours a day, is taxed at 25%. The fixture has no hours, so it cannot say which applies. Sage demo employee "marco" (a Sage demo record, not a real person). Sage tax status: temporary_part_time. Sage shows age 37 only; the date of birth is set to 1 January 1989 (year only kept). No case is near 65 (rebates) or 18-29 (ETI). Net is not on the Sage table: it is monthly pay less the Sage PAYE and employee UIF (no other deductions). ETI: nil by ETI Act s6(a), age outside 18-29. TS-b (wave 5): no hours are recorded for this case, so the engine classifies it as standard employment on the tables (R0.00) with a HOURS_NOT_RECORDED warning (casual); Sage's R1 125.00 stays a named gap (hours-blind Sage parity), replaced as a statutory proof by ts-standard-22h-boundary-tables-not-flat-25pct and ts-non-standard-under-5h-day-flat-25pct.
